newsitem.title: MADAGASCAR: Interim Madagascar president names new government.
newsitem.headline: Interim Madagascar president names new government.

text.p: Madagascar's interim president on Friday named a new government until a presidential election due in November, replacing among others an interior minister allied with impeached President Albert Zafy.
The new government announced by Norbert Ratsirahonana, who serves as interim president and prime minister, consists of 16 new ministers and 12 retained from Zafy's government.

Manahira Ranoharison was replaced as interior minister by Colonel Sylvain Rabotoarison of the gendarmerie. Rabotoarison held the same post during the transition from military ruler Didier Ratsiraka to multi-party politics in 1992.
The president said his new government reflected almost all regions of Madagascar, the world's fourth largest island off the south-east coast of Africa.

"Some members of government with ideas directly opposed to each other are in this team, but I am convinced that once they are in the cabinet, ministerial solidarity and the superior interest of the nation will prevail among them," he said.
The cabinet contains both supporters and opponents of Zafy, 70, who was impeached in July by parliament, citing repeated violations of the constitution and actions against the people's interests.
The impeachment was confirmed by the constitutional court on September 4.
Zafy, who became president in 1993, says he will run in the November 3 election, which is permitted by law despite his impeachment.
The impeachment capped three years of political instability on this Indian Ocean island with a population of 14 million.

Political infighting has frustrated efforts to get the economy moving. Madagascar hopes to conclude debt-rescheduling and lending agreements this month with the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.
